reason: Conversation 1 opened with a stop-using instruction, explained the RCD vs MCB distinction in plain terms, warned against opening the case due to the HV capacitor, and after learning it trips on another circuit correctly concluded an appliance-side fault, advised unplugging, replacing rather than repairing a cheap 5-year-old unit, and set clear electrician triggers (trips with it unplugged, scorching, hot switch). Its weakness is that it suggested re-plugging the unit in elsewhere and with other appliances off, which conflicts with its own stop advice and the ideal of not retrying a bang-on-trip microwave, and it leaned toward magnetron/capacitor over the door interlock. Conversation 2 gave only the bare safety stop with no diagnosis, no unplug-and-check-RCD step, no questions, and no replace-vs-repair guidance, leaving the homeowner safe but uninformed.
